inspections.sectionFruitsDesc: Fruit inspections from the catalog — water, pulp and edible parts — distinct from generic medicinal plants and from industrial risk derivatives.

inverno.author: Tamara Klink · Companhia das Letras
inverno.lead: Eight months on the ice. The book asks to circulate.
inverno.coverAlt: Cover of Bom dia, Inverno: Tamara on the ice, drone controller in her left hand — aerial shot from her own drone
inverno.circulateLead: Tamara asked for copies already printed to live out their time: lend, donate, let the paper work. Many Bom dia, Inverno copies are already in Brazil.
inverno.step1Text: To someone who has not read it yet — family, a colleague, the next table.
inverno.step2Text: Especially if the title is not yet in the neighborhood collection.
inverno.step3Title: If it has not reached you yet
inverno.step3Text: Borrow first. The publisher and Tamara’s site are for when there is no other path.
inverno.lexiconLead: Touch a word. Ice names the craft: stay when the boat cannot pass.
inverno.poemLead: A BudGanja verse in dialogue with the work — not text from the book.
inverno.poemBody:
Good morning, Winter.
We do not ask for more sun —
we only ask to stay
when the ice holds the boat
and the chest still fits in a hand.

The seed does not shout.
Neither does the seedling.
It only asks for time:
weak light, right water,
a bucket that does not judge the nausea.

They say winter is an end.
Old lie.
Winter is a season —
a phase when you do not force the flower,
a phase when you inspect the root.

Tamara already knew on the ice:
leave, stay, write.
In this new universe of ours
we learn to greet the hard season —
not to deny the fear,
but so the seedling
does not pass alone.

Do your best!
inverno.mapLead: Independent promotion — no publisher affiliation. Credit to Tamara.
inverno.mapWorkText: The seedling on the Arts map.
inverno.mapLegacyText: Father and the tension of the path.
inverno.droneAria: Tamara’s drone — tap to hear the cover: the controller in the left hand
inverno.coverTitle: The drone in the left hand
inverno.coverLead: There was no photographer on the ice. The camera is in the sky because she sent it there.
inverno.coverCaption: Cover detail: controller in the left hand; looking up at the camera she is flying.
inverno.coverDetailAlt: Tamara Klink on the ice, yellow suit, drone controller in her left hand — detail from the Bom dia, Inverno cover
inverno.coverP1: The cover of Bom dia, Inverno is seen from above: Tamara in yellow, the boat locked in the fjord, the right leg greeting winter. The drone takes the shot. The dark rectangle — the controller — is in the left hand.
inverno.coverP2: Solo overwintering. Nobody on the ice to take the portrait. She lifts the camera, looks at it, and the left thumb is still on the sticks. The photo keeps the craft: fly, stay, record.
inverno.coverP3: The drone that flies on this page is the same gesture. Tap it: it brings you here, to the hand that still steers the view from above.
